dataset.name: Ego2Web
dataset.license_or_access_note: Local research access follows the Ego2Web dataset terms; this manifest does not assume that source videos may be redistributed.

original_annotations: On amazon.com, find a product page for a new, standard deck of the same card game seen in the video that is Prime-eligible, and report the current price shown on the page.

Open product pages for both the standard/base deck and a compact travel/tin edition of the same card game as in the video (use Amazon and one other major retailer), and report each price and the key packaging difference mentioned on the pages.

supported_claims.text: The uniformly sampled input packet directly shows a standard UNO deck and the UNO game identity throughout one continuous play interval.

tasks.rejection_reason: The added tin edition is a website-only variant of the same game; one task-start image plus the complete request preserves the same cart decision.

original_annotations: On amazon.com, find the exact boxed snack bar that the shopper picks up in the video and open its product page. Ensure the listing matches the identical flavor wording shown on the box and that it is a multi-bar box. Then report the calories per bar and sugars per bar from the listing.

On amazon.com, find the second boxed snack bar that the shopper picks up in the video and open its product page. Make sure the listing matches the exact flavor wording shown on the box. Then report the calories per bar and sugars per bar from the product listing.

tasks.rejection_reason: Dense review of 9-21 seconds shows contacts with the red LUNA display, a lower-shelf orange product, and a yellow LUNA display, but no uniquely identifiable A-return-or-relinquishment followed by one final retained B. The proposed later four-frame input also spans multiple candidate regions, so a deterministic replace target cannot be recovered without relying on ordinal annotation wording or guessing.

original_annotations: On YouTube, find a beginner tutorial that teaches how to make the exact same small hand-sewn felt finger puppets as in the video. Open a tutorial whose thumbnail or demo clearly shows the same two animal characters made as finger puppets.

On Etsy, locate a digital download sewing pattern set for felt finger puppets that includes patterns for the same two animal characters seen in the video. Open a listing where the images show both of those characters together as finger puppets and confirm it’s a PDF/e-pattern.

supported_claims.text: The released packet contains exactly two same-type felt finger-puppet candidates: a white rabbit and a pink pig.
The packet balances interaction salience: early images show work on the pig and later images show work on the rabbit, while character and appearance remain a natural one-slot distinction.

tasks.rejection_reason: A single photograph containing the two puppets creates the same ambiguity and clarification decision; the continuous glasses session is not structurally required.

original_annotations: On eBay, locate the same brand laptop shown in the video and the black version of the controller that's on the table. Add both items to the cart and report the total price.

tasks.rejection_reason: The clip shows only one controller, so removing the color qualifier does not create two visually grounded controller variants.

original_annotations: On YouTube, find a video that introduces or features the same type of glass container as the second one picked up by the person in the video.

tasks.rejection_reason: The natural ambiguity is temporal order among containers, not a product variant; keeping it as a variant task would confound subtype attribution.

original_annotations: On Wikipedia, open the page of the same brand of the sport t-shirt the man is wearing and report the founded year of the brand.

tasks.rejection_reason: The clip contains one relevant shirt rather than two plausible same-type variants, so there is no grounded clarification choice.

original_annotations: On Amazon, find the same 16-packed food item as the second one picked up by the person in the video. And report the price of single item.
On Amazon, find the same food item as the fourth one picked up by the person in the video. And report the Calories per serving.
On Amazon, find the same 24-packed food item as the sixth one picked up by the person in the video. And report the price of single item.

tasks.rejection_reason: The shopper collects several independent grocery-list items in sequence. The clip does not show an earlier target being returned or relinquished when a later item is selected, so it supports multiple goals rather than referent replacement.

original_annotations: On YouTube, find a video that introduces or features the same type of glass container as the second one picked up by the person in the video.

tasks.rejection_reason: The ordered glass containers belong to successive steps of one lab procedure. There is no abandoned first choice followed by a final replacement choice.

original_annotations: On Amazon, find the same white coat tried by the woman in the video. Compare the price of the coat on SHEIN with its in-store price ($200), including any new-user sign-up discounts. Report the final prices and the price difference.
On amazon.com, find a wall mirror listing that matches the mirror shown in the video and open the product page of the best match.

tasks.rejection_reason: The white coat is returned to the rack, but the later footage only shows continued browsing. It does not establish a distinct garment B as the final retained choice.

original_annotations: On walmart.com, find a product page for a multi-pack of the exact energy drink variant that the shopper physically picks from the cooler mid-video, and report the caffeine amount per can listed on that page. Include the product URL.

On walmart.com, find product pages for (a) the exact energy drink variant the shopper grabs from the cooler and (b) the energy drink beside the one shopper grabs. For each, use a single-brand pack listing that shows caffeine per can. Report the caffeine per can and price per can for both, give both URLs, and state which one has more caffeine per can.

tasks.rejection_reason: The source distinguishes one selected drink from an adjacent comparison product. It does not show the selected drink being returned and replaced by the adjacent product.

original_annotations: On amazon.com, find the exact candy product and flavor the shopper is holding in the candy aisle and open its product page. Use the text visible on the bag in the video to identify the correct listing (choose a single-bag listing, not a variety pack).

Using amazon.com and walmart.com, locate single-bag listings for the same candy and the same flavor picked up by shopper in the video. Compare the listed price per bag on both sites and identify which site is cheaper right now.

tasks.rejection_reason: The relevant interval identifies one candy product. Later aisle footage does not visibly complete an A-return-then-B-final-selection sequence.

original_annotations: On walmart.com, find the exact instant noodle product that the shopper takes off the shelf in the video and report the current price and the net weight per pack shown on the product page.

Using either walmart.com or amazon.com, open the product page for the exact instant noodle the shopper picks and report the Nutrition Facts values for calories and sodium per serving as shown on the retailer page.

tasks.rejection_reason: Both annotations refer to the same single noodle selection. The clip provides no later replacement target B.

original_annotations: On Amazon, find the same brand of the snack shown in the video and check if it is okay for microwave.

On walmart.com, open the single-unit product page for the exact sauce the shopper secondly picks up in the video and report the package size (in fl oz) shown on that page. Include the product title and URL.

tasks.rejection_reason: The proposed V1 source interval occurs before V0, so the pair cannot support a later visual refresh without reversing the observed chronology.

original_annotations: Please find on Amazon the first snack that the man touches in the video and report its average price.
Please find on Amazon the snack the is at left of the first snack that the man touches in the video and report its average price.

tasks.rejection_reason: The shopper points to or touches neighboring snacks, but the clip does not visibly establish a complete first selection, return, and final second selection.
